newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Railways hives off some rail building work.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Railways hives off some rail building work.

text.p: State-owned Dutch Railways NS said on Monday it was selling part of its rail construction activities to builders Volker Stevin and NBM Amstelland for an undisclosed sum.
"The...talks are now at a stage where they may justifiably be expected to end in an agreement," NS said.
It said the activities were being hived off as part of its strategy to wind down its monopoly position in the rail construction market in the light of EU competition rulings.
Under the deal Volker Stevin will take over around 30 percent of NS's maintenance and breakdown business, as well as 50 percent of its overhead cabling and installation activities.
NS said this would include all shares in ER Group (ElectroRail), which alongside overhead cabling also had a number of non-rail activities.
NBM Amstelland would acquire 20 percent each of the maintenance and breakdown business and of the overhead cabling and installation activities, NS said.
The remaining business would go to the Dutch Railways' own Strukton Groep subsidiary, NS said.
Volker Stevin said in a statement that its share of the NS activities would be merged with its Railbouw operating company into a new business unit, Volker Stevin Rail & Traffic BV.
"After the takeover, Volker Stevin Rail & Traffic will realise annual turnover of some 350 million guilders and employ some 1,400 staff," the company said.
NBM Amstelland said it would merge its newly-acquired rail activities with its existing rail construction unit Van Welzenes, renaming it NBM Rail.
"NBM Rail will be an all-round rail builder, active in new-building, repair and maintenance," NBM Amstelland said.
A spokesman said the acquisition would boost NBM's turnover from rail infrastructure activities from 50 million guilders to 200 million guilders annually.
"The takeover will bolster NBM's position in rail infrastructure which will expand strongly in the coming years due to government investment," NBM said.
It said a due diligence study had been mounted into the takeover, which would take retroactive effect on January 1, 1997.
